name: Saltwall Numbers — The Shelf Daily Draw
description: Saltwall Numbers is a hand-run daily lottery operating across the Shelf's eastern districts, drawing on a three-digit system with roots in pre-Collapse informal economies. Players place bets through a network of corner runners — mostly teenagers and elders — who collect slips and Quanta before each day's draw, which is conducted publicly at the Saltwall After Dark canteen and broadcast on pirate mesh. A Φ1 straight bet on the correct three digits pays Φ600; combination bets and partial matches have scaled returns. The operation is managed by a loose cooperative of district elders who reinvest a fixed percentage of proceeds into neighborhood emergency funds.
story_hooks: The numbers draw has come up the same three digits four times in thirty days — statistically impossible — and no one can agree whether the fix is in or something stranger is happening.

A city enforcement unit has been tasked with shutting down Saltwall Numbers as part of a 'district modernization' push that everyone on the Shelf knows is really about clearing land for a Tier 3 development.
One of the teenage runners has been skimming — not out of greed, but to fund something the neighborhood might actually want if they knew about it.
